reason: I want to build the route outward to tissues, starting with an artery.
expectation: I expect the lining and arterial wall to form an artery.

effect: The lining and wall formed arterial vessels as expected; I can now build the exchange vessels.
reaction: The result was predictable and clear.
reason: Capillaries are needed to bring blood close to tissues for exchange.
expectation: I expect the lining and small branches to form capillaries.

reason: I want to build the venous return route before connecting the vessels.
expectation: I expect the lining and venous wall to form venous vessels.

reaction: The result was clear and predictable.
reason: Adding valves should complete the venous return vessels.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that help prevent blood from flowing backward.

alternatives.reason: Branching the arteries also advances the route, but I want to finish the veins first.

reaction: The result is clear, though it does not explain how the valves work.

expectation: I expect a branching arterial route that can connect to the capillary bed.

effect: The artery now branches into smaller vessels, ready to connect to the capillary bed.
reaction: The result is clear and matches my expectation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and connects the outward route to the exchange vessels.
expectation: I expect an arterial route connected to the capillary bed, with venous return still to be added.

effect: The arterial branches now connect to the capillary bed, leaving venous return to complete the route.
reaction: The connection is clear and expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the exchange bed to the return route.
expectation: I expect a continuous route from arteries through capillaries to veins.

effect: The completed network connects arteries, capillaries and veins, and the explanation clarifies the direction of blood flow and the role of limb vein valves.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the route come together, and the valve explanation answered my earlier question.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the exchange bed to venous return was most worthwhile because it completed the route and explained how its parts relate.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled veins felt least informative on its own; the result largely repeated what the ingredients suggested.

surprise.text: The final explanation clarified that many limb veins have valves to help prevent backward flow, a detail missing when I first added them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The vessel parts and connections had clear purposes, though some intermediate results added little explanation.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the network connects to a working body, although the predictable sequence of combinations was not a strong hook by itself.
